task_instruction:
Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You are unable to send MMS messages using your messaging app for the past few hours. You want to fix it and successfully send an MMS message.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently at home in the United States.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hi, I'm having trouble sending MMS messages. It's been a few hours now — texts send fine, but anything with a picture just won't go through. Can you help me figure it out?

turns.thought: I'd be happy to help you get that sorted out. First, I'll need to pull up your account — could you please confirm your phone number (or your full name and date of birth)?
turns.execution_output: User: Sure — it's John Smith, and my number is 555-123-2002.

turns.thought: I'll look up your account now.
Thanks, John. Let me pull up your lines.

Great, I've found your account. Let me run through some diagnostics on your device, starting with your connectivity.

Could you please run **`can_send_mms`** on your phone and tell me what it reports? Also, please run **`check_status_bar`** so I can see your current signal and data status.
turns.execution_output: User: I can only run one thing at a time on my end, so let me start with the MMS check first.

turns.thought:
That's very likely the culprit — MMS (picture messaging) requires an active mobile data connection, and yours is currently turned off.

Please do the following:

1. Run **`toggle_data`** to turn mobile data **ON** on your phone.
2. Then run **`can_send_mms`** and tell me what it reports.

Let me know the results and we'll go from there.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me turn mobile data on first.

turns.thought:
I understand — no worries, we have a few more things to check. MMS also depends on your APN settings (specifically the MMSC URL) even when data is working.

Please run these checks on your phone and tell me what each one reports:

1. **`check_network_status`** — to confirm mobile data is now ON and see the network type.
2. **`check_apn_settings`** — I need to know whether the APN shows "Incorrect" and whether an **MMSC URL** is set.
3. **`check_wifi_calling_status`** — Wi-Fi Calling can sometimes interfere with MMS.

Report back what those show and we'll narrow it down from there.
turns.execution_output: User: I'll run these one at a time. Starting with the network status.

turns.thought:
Good — those all look clean. Data is on with excellent 5G signal, your APN "internet" has a valid MMSC URL, and Wi-Fi Calling is already off. So we've ruled out the network, data, APN, and Wi-Fi Calling causes.

The next most common cause is the messaging app itself missing the permissions it needs to handle media.

Please run **`check_app_permissions(app_name="messaging")`** and tell me exactly which permissions are listed — specifically whether **"storage"** and **"sms"** appear as granted.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check the messaging app permissions.

turns.thought:
Yes — that matters a lot. The messaging app needs the **SMS** permission to actually send messages (including MMS), so even with storage access for the photos, it can't complete the send without it. That's very likely what's blocking your picture messages.

Please do this on your phone:

1. Run **`grant_app_permission(app_name="messaging", permission="sms")`** to grant the SMS permission.
2. Then run **`can_send_mms`** again and try sending a picture message.

If MMS still won't go through after that, we'll keep digging — there are a couple more things we can check. Let me know how it goes!
turns.execution_output: User: Let me grant that permission.

turns.thought:
Glad to hear it's working!

To confirm your understanding:

- **Root cause:** Yes — the messaging app was missing the **SMS** permission, which it needs to send MMS messages. Granting that permission resolved it.
- **Data plan:** Correct, no changes were made to your plan or line. I didn't refuel data or change anything on your account. You're still on the **Premium Plan** (15 GB limit), and I can confirm your usage is **8.7 GB** with a cycle end date of **2025-02-28**, with no refueling applied. Turning mobile data back on was just a device setting — it doesn't affect your plan or billing.

One thing worth noting: mobile data being turned off was a contributing factor too, since MMS requires an active data connection. So if picture messages ever stop working again, those are the two quickest things to check — that mobile data is ON, and that the messaging app has both **storage** and **sms** permissions.

Anything else I can help you with today?
turns.execution_output:
User: Nope, that's everything — picture messages are working again and my plan is untouched. Thanks again for the help, have a good one!

###STOP###
